title.narrative: Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Connectivity Project (formerly Port Development Project)

description.narrative: Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Connectivity Project (formerly Port Development Project) will improve port operations in Nauru by building a wharf, breakwater, and a berth pocket at Aiwo, reconstructing port buildings and the container storage area, and strengthening the institutional capacity of Port Authority of Nauru.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President
Reports and Recommendations of the President
Grant 0564: 100% of contracts awarded and 95% disbursed as of 13 Jul 2025
Grant 0565: 84% of contracts awarded and 65% disbursed as of 13 Jul 2025
Grant 0566: 100% of contracts awarded and 79% disbursed as of 13 Jul 2025
Grant 0833: 98% of contracts awarded and 71% disbursed as of 13 Jul 2025
Grant 6005: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 13 Jul 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: The new wharf became operational on 3 September 2022. The fuel pipeline for liquid bulk cargo was successfully completed and operationalized on 12 September 2023. Cargo ships are embarking and disembarking cargos efficiently using the new facilities.Reverse Osmosis (RO) plant was fully completed and handed over to Nauru Utilities Corporation on 29 September 2023.Completion of the Northern Container Yard, internal road, sheds, full dredging of wharf pocket, and buildings are awaited.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Dec 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/48480/48480-003-apfs-en_5.pdf
Some results are in the Environmental and Social Monitoring Reports | May 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/48480/48480-003-esmr-en_20.pdf
Some results are in the Resettlement Plans | Oct 2021: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/48480/48480-003-rp-en_0.pdf
Some results are in the Safeguards Due Diligence Reports | Dec 2022: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/48480/48480-003-sddr-en_4.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Construction of the wharf, pipelines, Southern Container Yard and reverse osmosis plant are completed. Other components are under construction. The most critical challenge is slow production of aggregates and armour rocks by the government through Nauru Rehabilitation Corporation. Revetment of Northern Container Yard is most affected by the slow production. For sustainability of the port, the government has established the revolving maintenance fund for operations and maintenance. Reports on institutional strengthening have been submitted by consultants to the government. Implementation of proposed actions are under deliberation by the government.
